q: 1. The property of fresh concrete, in which the water in the mix tends to rise to the surface while placing and compacting, is called ...........
explain: Bleeding is a form of segregation where water comes out to the surface of the concrete because it has the lowest specific gravity among the ingredients.

q: 2. The property of the ingredients to separate from each other while placing the concrete is called ...........
explain: Segregation is the separation of constituent materials of concrete, usually resulting in the coarse aggregate settling or separating from the matrix.

q: 3. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to ...........
explain: Better grading of aggregate reduces voids and internal friction, thereby increasing the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 4. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to ...........
explain: As the time of transit increases, concrete loses moisture due to evaporation and hydration, causing workability to decrease.

q: 5. Approximate value of shrinkage strain in concrete, is ...........
explain: In the absence of specific data, the design value for total shrinkage strain is taken as 0.0003 as per IS:456.

q: 6. Air entrainment in the concrete increases ...........
explain: Air entraining agents create minute air bubbles that act like ball bearings, significantly increasing the workability of the mix.

q: 7. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr, splitting strength fcs and direct tensile strength ft is given by ...........
explain: The modulus of rupture (flexural strength) is always highest, followed by splitting tensile strength, with direct tensile strength being the lowest.

q: 8. The approximate value of the ratio between direct tensile strength and flexural strength is
explain: Direct tensile strength is typically about 50% (0.5) of the flexural strength (modulus of rupture).

q: 9. Strength of concrete increases with ...........
explain: Finer cement provides more surface area for hydration, leading to a more rapid development of strength.

q: 10. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and characteristic strength of concrete fck is given by ...........
explain: As per IS:456, the flexural strength of concrete is calculated using the formula 0.7 * sqrt(fck).

q: 11. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always ...........
explain: Smaller specimen sizes usually exhibit higher apparent compressive strength because of reduced probability of critical flaws and different end-restraint effects.

q: 12. According to I.S.: 456-1978, the modulus of elasticity of concrete Ec (in N/mm2) can be taken as ...........
explain: The older version of the code (IS 456:1978) specified 5700 * sqrt(fck); note that the 2000 version uses 5000 * sqrt(fck).

q: 13. Increase in the moisture content in concrete ...........
explain: Higher moisture content beyond the required water-cement ratio increases the volume of voids once evaporated, thus reducing strength.

q: 14. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzolanic cement ...........
explain: Pozzolanic cements generally show higher drying shrinkage compared to Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC).

q: 15. Admixtures which cause early setting, and hardening of concrete are called ...........
explain: Accelerators are chemicals that speed up the chemical reaction of cement with water, reducing setting time and increasing early strength.

q: 16. The most commonly use admixture which prolongs the setting and hardening time is ...........
explain: Gypsum is added during cement manufacturing to act as a retarder, preventing the 'flash set' of C3A.

q: 17. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately ...........
explain: Standard bulk cement usually contains roughly 40% voids by volume in its loose state.

q: 18. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about ...........
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength over time due to slow hydration; after one year, it is typically 20-25% stronger than at 28 days.

q: 19. As compared to ordinary portland cement, high alumina cement has ...........
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial and final setting times
lower initial and final setting times
explain: High Alumina Cement (HAC) is characterized by a high initial setting time but a very rapid final setting and hardening process.

q: 20. Modulus of rupture of concrete is a measure of ...........
explain: The modulus of rupture is the theoretical maximum tensile stress reached in the bottom fiber of a test beam during a flexure test.

q: 21. In reinforced cement concrete structures, the steel reinforcement consists of ...........
options: mild steel and medium tensile steel bars
explain: Reinforced concrete can utilize various types of steel reinforcement including mild steel, CTD, and modern TMT (deformed) bars.

q: 22. A twisted bar has about ........... more yield stress than ordinary mild steel bar.
explain: Cold twisting increases the yield strength of the steel by approximately 50% due to the strain hardening effect.

q: 23. In the limit state method, the compressive force in concrete is taken to act at a distance of ...... times the neutral axis measured from the extreme compression fibre.
explain: Based on the parabolic-rectangular stress block used in IS:456, the centroid of the compressive force is 0.42 times the depth of the neutral axis (xu).

q: 24. The surface width of cracks shall not generally exceed ...........
explain: For members under moderate exposure conditions, the maximum crack width is limited to 0.3 mm to ensure durability.

q: 25. As per I.S.: 456-1978, the pH value of water shall be ...........
explain: Water used for mixing and curing concrete must be clean and have a pH value not less than 6 to avoid acidic attack on the concrete.

q: 26. The nominal shear stress in beams of M 15 grade concrete (even with shear reinforcement) under no circumstances shall exceed ...........
explain: The maximum shear stress (τc max) for M15 grade concrete is 2.5 N/mm² to prevent diagonal compression failure.

q: 27. The increase in strength of concrete after six months is generally ...........
explain: Over a six-month period, the continuous hydration of cement typically adds about 20% to the 28-day strength.

q: 28. Modular ratio in reinforced concrete is defined as ...........
options: Modulus of elasticity of steel / Modulus of elasticity of concrete
Modulus of elasticity of concrete / Modulus of elasticity of steel
Coefficient of linear expansion steel / Coefficient of linear expansion of concrete
explain: Modular ratio (m) is the ratio of the Modulus of Elasticity of Steel (Es) to the Modulus of Elasticity of Concrete (Ec).

q: 29. Working loads may be defined as ...........
options: maximum loads consisting of dead and live loads
a set of critical loads in service conditions
all loads that occur during service conditions
a set of maximum loads for which no failure will occur
explain: Working loads (service loads) are the actual loads expected to occur on the structure during its normal life.

q: 30. The decrease in stress caused in a pre-stressed beam at constant strain is called ...........
explain: Relaxation is the time-dependent decrease of stress in steel held at a constant strain.

q: 31. An increase in strain in a concrete member at constant stress is called ...........
explain: Creep is the property of concrete by which it continues to deform (increase in strain) over time under a sustained constant load or stress.

q: 32. Strain in concrete at zero stress is called ...........
explain: Shrinkage is the time-dependent strain in concrete resulting from the loss of water, which occurs regardless of the external loading/stress.

q: 33. M 10 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: Standard nominal mix proportions for M10 concrete is 1 part cement, 3 parts fine aggregate, and 6 parts coarse aggregate.

q: 34. M 15 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: M15 concrete is typically mixed in the ratio of 1:2:4 (Cement:Sand:Aggregate).

q: 35. M 20 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: The nominal mix for M20 concrete is 1:1.5:3, providing a characteristic strength of 20 N/mm².

q: 36. M 25 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: For M25, the nominal mix is approximately 1:1:2, though higher grades usually require design mixes.

q: 37. The maintenance cost of concrete structures is ...........
options: as much as for timber structures
explain: Unlike steel or timber, concrete does not rust or rot easily, making its long-term maintenance costs very low.

q: 38. The reason for choosing mild steel bars as reinforcement in tensile zones of concrete is that ...........
options: The modulus of elasticity of mild steel is about the same as that of concrete
The Poisson's ratio of mild steel is almost the same as that of concrete
The coefficient of linear expansion is about the same as that of concrete
The stress-strain plots of both mild steel and concrete are identical in shape
explain: Steel and concrete expand and contract at nearly the same rate with temperature changes, preventing internal bond failure.

q: 39. The advantage of concrete is that ...........
options: it can be moulded into any shape and size
it is durable and maintenance cost is practically nil
explain: Concrete is versatile, durable, and naturally fire-resistant, offering all these structural benefits.

q: 40. The probability that the actual strength of the material is more than its characteristic strength is ...........
explain: Characteristic strength is defined as the value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall, meaning 95% are above it.

q: 41. In the limit state design, the strength of concrete as well as the strength of steel is taken to be a random variable that follows ...........
explain: Structural engineering codes assume a Normal (Gaussian) distribution for the frequency of material strength results.

q: 42. The chances for the actual strength of concrete to be less than its characteristic strength are ...........
explain: By definition, the characteristic strength (fck) allows for a 5% probability of failure (strength being lower than fck).

q: 43. Compared to plain bars, the deformed bars will have ...........
explain: Deformed bars (HYSD) provide mechanical interlocking for better bond and higher yield strength, leading to reduced steel consumption.

q: 44. The modulus of elasticity of steel is generally taken as ...........
explain: The standard value for the modulus of elasticity of all types of reinforcing steel is 200 kN/mm² or 200,000 N/mm².

q: 45. The design load obtained after multiplying the characteristic load by the partial safety factor is also known as ...........
explain: In Limit State Design, the design load is the factored load (Characteristic Load x γf).

q: 46. In terms of the mean load Fm and the standard deviation of the load Fs, the characteristic load Fk is given by ...........
explain: Characteristic load is the value that has a 95% probability of not being exceeded during the life of the structure.

q: 47. According to I.S.: 456, the thickness of R.C.C. footing on soils at its edges is kept not less than ...........
explain: To ensure durability and proper cover, IS:456 specifies a minimum edge thickness of 150 mm for footings on soil.

q: 48. According to I.S.: 456, the thickness at the edge on top of piles for a footing on the piles should not be less than ...........
explain: For footings on piles, the minimum edge thickness is increased to 300 mm due to the higher concentrated loads from piles.

q: 49. For calculating the depth of an isolated sloped footing of width "b" for a column of size "a", the width of the footing is taken as ...........
explain: This is a simplified geometric approximation used for determining effective width in sloped footing calculations.

q: 50. If the width of the foundation for two columns is restricted, the shape of the footing generally adopted is ...........
explain: A trapezoidal combined footing is used when the load of one column is much higher than the other and the width of the footing is restricted.

q: 51. In a combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging bending moment will occur ...........
explain: In combined footings, the shear force diagram typically crosses zero (maximum moment) near the heavier load point.

q: 52. One way shear strength in a R.C.C. footing is checked at a distance equal to ........... of the footing from the face of the column
explain: One-way shear (beam shear) is checked at a critical section at distance 'd' from the column face.

q: 53. Two way shear strength in a R.C.C. footing is checked at a distance equal to ........... of the footing from the face of the column along the surface of truncated cone ...........
explain: Two-way shear (punching shear) is checked at a critical section at a distance of 'd/2' from the column face.

q: 54. The critical section for checking the development length in a footing shall be at the same planes as for ...........
options: one way and two way shear
explain: The critical section for development length is the same as for bending moment (at the face of the column).

q: 55. The zone in which transverse bending is likely to occur may be obtained by drawing a line from the faces to the column making an angle 'θ' with the horizontal where 'θ' may be ...........
explain: A 45-degree dispersion is commonly assumed for the distribution of loads and stresses in thick concrete elements like footings.

q: 56. A raft foundation is provided if the areas of the foundation exceeds the plan area of the building by ...........
explain: If individual footings cover more than 50% of the building area, a raft (mat) foundation is usually more economical and safer.

q: 57. In a combined footing, the bottom bars under a column should be extended in to the interior of the slab. This distance should be greater of the distance up to the point of contraflexure and ...........
options: 30 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the outer face of the column
42 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the outer face of the column
30 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the inner face of the column
42 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the inner face of the column
explain: Standard detailing rules for development and anchorage require a minimum extension (often 42d for specific steel grades) beyond critical sections.

q: 58. Pile foundations are normally used ...........
options: when the bearing area require is not available
explain: Piles are used when surface soil is weak or when the space is too limited to provide a large shallow foundation.

q: 59. Pile foundations are invariably used in ...........
explain: Due to high water tables and heavy structural loads, bridge piers almost always utilize pile foundations for stability.

q: 60. A square column of side a is founded on a square footing is side b. The maximum bending moment on the footing corresponding to a net upward pressure p is given by ...........
explain: Derived from treating the cantilever portion of the footing as a beam: $M =  rac{p \cdot ( rac{b-a}{2})^2}{2}$ per unit width.

q: 61. If the allowable punching shear stress is q, the depth of footing from punching shear criterion to carry a load W is given by ...........
explain: This formula relates total load, footing area, column area, and the punching shear perimeter to solve for required depth.

q: 62. A foundation rests on ...........
explain: Subgrade and foundation soil are terms used to describe the natural or prepared ground that supports the foundation load.

q: 63. For a number of columns constructed in a row, the type of foundation provided, is ...........
explain: A strip footing is a continuous foundation used to support a row of columns or a wall.

q: 64. On an absolutely rigid foundation base, the pressure will ...........
options: be more at the edge of the foundation
be zero at the centre of the foundation
explain: Theory assumes that a perfectly rigid foundation on a perfectly elastic soil results in a uniform pressure distribution.

q: 65. To ensure uniform pressure distribution, the thickness of the foundation, is ...........
explain: Varying the thickness (as in sloped or stepped footings) helps distribute the stiffness and pressure more effectively.

q: 66. The self-weight of the footing is ...........
options: not considered for calculating the upward pressure on footing
also considered for calculating the upward pressure on footing
not considered for calculating the area of the footing
explain: Self-weight acts downwards and is counteracted directly by the soil, so it is not included in the 'net' upward pressure used for designing the concrete section.

q: 67. Ina combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging bending moment occurs at ...........
options: a point equidistant from either column
a point of the maximum shear force
a point of zero shear force
explain: From basic mechanics, the maximum bending moment (hogging or sagging) always occurs where the shear force is zero.

q: 68. In a combined footing if shear stress does not exceed 5 kg/cm², the nominal stirrups provided are ...........
explain: For large combined footings, 8-legged stirrups are often a minimum requirement for nominal shear reinforcement.

q: 69. In a combined footing if shear stress exceed 5 kg/cm², the nominal stirrups provided are ...........
explain: As shear stress increases, more legs are required in the stirrup arrangement to effectively resist the diagonal tension.

q: 70. Top bars are extended to the projecting parts of the combined footing of two columns L distance apart for a distance ...........
options: 0.1 L from the outer edge of column
0.1 L from the centre edge of column
explain: This detailing rule ensures that top reinforcement (for hogging moments) is properly anchored into the cantilever projection.

q: 71. A compression member is termed as column or strut if the ratio of its effective length to the least lateral dimension is more than ...........
explain: If the slenderness ratio (Le/d) is less than 3, the member is considered a pedestal rather than a column.

q: 72. In the limit state method, the maximum strain in concrete in bending compression is taken to be ...........
explain: IS:456 specifies that the maximum compressive strain in the outermost fiber of concrete in bending is 0.0035.

q: 73. The design strength of the materials in the limit state method is given by ...........
explain: Design strength = Characteristic Strength (f) divided by Partial Safety Factor (γm).

q: 74. All columns shall be designed for an eccentricity not less than ...........
explain: Even if a column is nominally axially loaded, a minimum eccentricity of 20 mm must be considered to account for construction tolerances.

q: 75. When a vertical member is carrying mainly axial loads, it is termed as a ...........
explain: While 'strut' is a general term for compression members, 'column' specifically refers to vertical compression members in buildings.

q: 76. The shape of a column should be ...........
explain: Columns can be designed in any shape (square, rectangle, circle, L-shape, T-shape) depending on the architectural and structural needs.

q: 77. When the ratio of effective length of the column to its least lateral dimension does not exceed 12, it is termed as a ...........
explain: A column is classified as short if its slenderness ratio (Le/d) is 12 or less (Note: some older texts used 15, but 12 is the standard).

q: 78. While designing a reinforced concrete pole as a column, it is considered as ...........
options: fixed at one end and hinged at the other end
explain: R.C.C. poles are generally embedded deep in the ground, providing a fixed-end condition at the base and continuity at the top.

q: 79. The purpose of lateral ties in short reinforced concrete columns is to ...........
options: increase the load carrying capacity of the column
explain: Lateral ties provide lateral support to the longitudinal bars to prevent them from buckling outward under high axial loads.

q: 80. A long column is one whose ratio of effective length to its least lateral dimension exceeds ...........
explain: If the ratio of effective length to least lateral dimension (Le/d) exceeds 12, it is classified as a long (slender) column.

q: 81. In a column, with helical reinforcement, the permissible load is based on the core area. The least lateral dimension of such a column should be taken as ...........
options: equal to the diameter of core
explain: In a helically reinforced column, the 'core' is the concrete area enclosed within the center-line of the helical reinforcement, and its diameter defines the least lateral dimension for specific calculations.

q: 82. The area of longitudinal steel reinforcement in a column should not be ...........
options: less than 0.8% of the area of concrete section required for direct load alone
more than 6% of the gross sectional are of column
explain: IS:456 mandates a minimum of 0.8% (to prevent buckling and shrinkage cracks) and a maximum of 6% (to avoid congestion, though 4% is preferred for practical casting).

q: 83. The diameter of the polygonal links or lateral ties should not be less than....... of the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar ...........
explain: To provide adequate lateral restraint, the tie diameter must be at least one-fourth (1/4) the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar.

q: 84. The diameter of lateral ties, in no case, shall be less than ...........
explain: Regardless of the longitudinal bar size, the minimum absolute diameter for lateral ties is 5 mm (often rounded to 6 mm or 8 mm in modern practice).

q: 85. For a longitudinal reinforcing bar in a column, the cover should not be less than ...........
explain: A clear cover of 40 mm is required for columns to protect the steel from corrosion and fire, or the diameter of the bar if it is larger than 40 mm.

q: 86. A compression member is considered as short when both the slenderness ratio lex/D and ley/b are less than ...........
explain: A column is classified as short if the ratio of effective length to the corresponding lateral dimension is less than 12.

q: 87. The effective length of column with one and effectively held in position and other restrained against rotation at both directions is ...........
explain: For a column with both ends fixed against rotation and position, the theoretical value is 0.5l, but the design (recommended) value is 0.65l.

q: 88. The effective length of a column with both ends effectively held in position, but not restrained against rotation is ...........
explain: For a column with both ends hinged (held in position but free to rotate), the effective length is equal to the unsupported length 'l'.

q: 89. A column is regarded as long column if the ration of its effective length to least lateral radius of gyration is more than ...........
explain: A slenderness ratio (l/r) greater than 60 indicates a long column likely to fail by buckling before reaching its crushing strength.

q: 90. The minimum eccentricity that should be used in the design of any R.C.C. column is given by ...........
explain: IS:456 specifies emin = (L/500) + (D/30), but not less than 20 mm, to account for misalignments.

q: 91. The minimum percentage of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. columns is ...........
explain: A minimum of 0.8% steel is necessary to help handle accidental eccentricity and shrinkage stresses in the concrete.

q: 92. The maximum percentage of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. columns is ...........
explain: Though 4% is common in practice to allow for lapping, the maximum theoretical limit is 6.0% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 93. The minimum diameter of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. column should not be less than ...........
explain: Main longitudinal bars in a column must have a minimum diameter of 12 mm to ensure sufficient stiffness for the cage.

q: 94. The minimum accidental eccentricity in axially loaded columns may occur due to ...........
explain: Accidental eccentricity accounts for construction defects, non-homogeneity of concrete, and uncertainty in end fixation.

q: 95. Transverse reinforcement in columns ...........
explain: Ties/links primarily prevent buckling of the main bars and confine the core; they are not directly accounted for in axial load capacity calculations.

q: 96. A column is a structural element that supports axial compression load and has a height equal t at least ...........
explain: By definition, if the ratio of the effective length to the least lateral dimension is less than 3, it's a pedestal, not a column.

q: 97. The effective length of column is taken as ...........
options: the distance between the ends of column
twice the length between ends of column
the half length between the ends of column
the distance between the points of contra flexure
explain: The effective length (Le) is the distance between adjacent points of zero moment (points of contraflexure) in the buckling shape.

q: 98. In limit state design, the relationship between stress strain distribution in concrete is assumed to be ...........
explain: IS:456 assumes a stress-strain curve for concrete that is parabolic up to 0.002 strain and constant thereafter up to 0.0035 strain.

q: 99. The ratio of minimum area of cross section of longitudinal bars and gross sectional area of column shall be ...........
explain: Since the minimum percentage is 0.8%, this corresponds to 0.8/100, which simplifies to 1/125.

q: 100. To provide sufficient rigidity in the column while fixing and concreting, the reinforced bars should not be less than ...........
explain: Bars smaller than 12 mm lack the structural rigidity required to withstand the forces of concrete pouring and vibration without shifting.
